63-013.r: Gandhiji's idea for family planning → self-control, the best means.

63-014.r: Gandhiji lived about 21 years in South Africa: went in 1893 at age 24 (Dada Abdullah's case), returned to India January 1915.

63-015.r: Gandhi returned from South Africa → January 1915; accepted Gopal Krishna Gokhale as his political mentor.

63-016.r: Gandhi thrown out of train at Pietermaritzburg despite first-class ticket (1893), on Durban to Pretoria trip for Dada Abdullah.

63-017.r: Gandhi first attended a Congress session → Calcutta Session, 1901.

63-018.r: Sabarmati (Satyagraha) Ashram → outskirts of Ahmedabad; first at Kocharab Bungalow of Jivanlal Desai, moved for farming space on 17 June 1917.

63-020.r: Oldest Gandhi ashram → Phoenix Ashram (1904, land near Phoenix station), his first ashram; reopened 27 February 2000.
63-020.t: Don't pick Sabarmati, Wardha or Sadaqat; Phoenix came first.

63-021.r: Gandhi adopted 'Seva Dharma' in South Africa → served poor patients in Rustumji's charity hospital as compounder; nursed wounded Boer War soldiers.

63-022.r: South African struggles prepared Gandhi to lead national movement (A true); R wrong → his struggle there was non-violent Satyagraha, not militancy.

63-023.r: Gandhi's 'Political Guru' → Gopal Krishna Gokhale; Gokhale visited South Africa in 1912 at Gandhi's invitation.

63-024.r: For Gandhi, politics = activity for public (social) welfare; key idea → decentralisation of power through village Panchayats.

63-025.r: Gandhian political model = morality (ethics) + religion + humanity; no place for authority → aimed at a Stateless Society.

63-026.r: Batak Mian, cook of indigo manager Erwin, refused to poison Gandhi's milk during Champaran Satyagraha (1917), saving him; Rajendra Prasad corroborated it.

63-028.r: 'Satyagraha' coined by Mahatma Gandhi; nephew Maganlal Gandhi first suggested 'Sada Graha' in a competition, Gandhi improved it.

63-029.r: Satyagraha = Satya (truth) + Agraha (insistence); first started by Mahatma Gandhi; Champaran 1917 → his first successful Satyagraha in India.

63-030.r: Champaran Satyagraha 1917 (Bihar, against forced indigo) → Gandhi's first Civil Disobedience in India; went on Raj Kumar Shukla's invitation.

63-031.r: Tinkathia system (Champaran) → ryot had to grow indigo on 3 kathas per beegha, i.e. 3/20th of his holding, at a fixed price.
63-031.h: Tin = three: three kathas out of 20 per beegha.

63-032.r: Gandhi best known for passive (inactive) resistance to win Independence; later called it Satyagraha (moral power) versus passive resistance (political tool).

63-033.r: Gandhi: 'destruction is the best method of dealing with foreign clothes', linking it to national self-respect.

63-034.r: Gandhi's boycott of British goods worked because Britain saw India as a major market for manufactured goods.

63-035.r: Order: Champaran Satyagraha (1917) → Ahmedabad Mill strike (February-March 1918) → Kheda Satyagraha (March-June 1918) → Non-Cooperation (1920-1922).
63-035.h: C-A-K-N: 'CAKe Now' = Champaran, Ahmedabad, Kheda, Non-Cooperation.

63-036.r: Gandhi first used hunger strike as a weapon → Ahmedabad mill strike (1918).

63-037.r: Order: Champaran (1917, indigo) → Ahmedabad Mill Strike (plague bonus) → Kheda (taxes despite crop failure) → Rowlatt Satyagraha.

63-038.r: Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India → Champaran, 1917.

63-039.r: Gandhi: born 2 October 1869, Porbandar; early education Rajkot; married Kasturba at 13; law at Inner Temple, London; most influenced by Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' → all true.

63-040.r: Ruskin's 'Unto This Last' (read in South Africa) → 'The good of the individual is contained in the good of all' → Gandhi's 'Welfare of all'.

63-041.r: Gandhian thought influenced by all → Ruskin (respect for physical labour), Thoreau (essay on Civil Disobedience), Tolstoy ('The kingdom of God is within you').

63-042.r: Swadeshi Movement (1905-1911, against Bengal partition) → not related to Gandhi, then in South Africa; Khilafat, Individual Satyagraha, Quit India were led by him.

63-043.r: Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) → led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, not Gandhi; Gandhi led Kheda (1918), Civil Disobedience (1930), Quit India (1942).

63-044.r: Gandhi → worked for untouchables ('Service to Harijans', weekly Harijan), launched Non-Cooperation and began Civil Disobedience → all correct.

63-045.r: First to call Gandhi 'Father of Nation' → Subhash Chandra Bose, on Azad Hind Radio from Rangoon, July 1944.

63-046.r: Prefix 'Mahatma' added to Gandhi during Champaran Satyagraha → by Rabindranath Tagore.
63-046.t: Don't confuse: Tagore → 'Mahatma'; Subhash Chandra Bose → 'Father of Nation'.

63-048.r: Gandhi's secretary during Noakhali → Pyare Lal (also in Dandi March); his sister Dr. Susheela Nayyar was Gandhi's personal doctor.

63-049.r: Vaikom Satyagraha → Gandhi did not take part directly; he led Rajkot (4-day hunger strike), Kheda and Non-Cooperation.

63-050.r: Vaikom Satyagraha (Travancore, Kerala) → temple entry for depressed classes, against untouchability and caste discrimination; Gandhi participated indirectly in 1925 (book: both correct).
63-050.t: Gandhi's role was only indirect; in 'not participated directly' questions, Vaikom is the answer.

63-051.r: Gandhi first came to Chhattisgarh on 20 December 1920 (Dhamtari); again on 24 November 1933.

63-052.r: J.B. Kripalani → teacher by profession among Gandhian followers; Rajendra Prasad taught briefly but was basically a lawyer.

63-053.r: Jamnalal Bajaj → capitalist and full-time Congress activist; AICC treasurer for many years; jailed in 1923 and 1930.

63-054.r: Jamnalal Bajaj → cotton merchant, banker, Congressman and close Gandhi associate; Gandhi called him his 'fifth son'.

63-055.r: Charles Andrews ('Deenbandhu') → Gandhi's close English compatriot; professor at St. Stephen's College, Delhi; lived at Phoenix Farm; later AITUC President.

63-056.r: Gandhi's Chhattisgarh tour 1920 → accompanied by Maulana Shaukat Ali (Khilafat leader); invited by Sundarlal Sharma.

63-057.r: Gandhi called Yerawada Central Jail (Pune) a 'Mandir'.

63-058.r: At Independence Gandhi was not a Congress member → resigned in 1934 and never formally rejoined.

63-059.r: 'The light has gone out of our lives' → Jawaharlal Nehru on Gandhi's murder by Nathuram Godse (30 January 1948).

63-060.r: Mountbatten called Gandhi the 'One-man Boundary Force' → Punjab had 50,000 soldiers yet riots; Bengal had one man and no rioting.

63-061.r: Gokhale (Gandhi's political Guru) asked him to spend his first year in India as observer, 'with his ears open but his mouth shut'.

63-063.r: 'Wrong means never take us to right ends' → M.K. Gandhi; means and ends are two sides of a coin.

63-064.r: 'What is morally wrong can never be politically right' → principle strongly upheld by M.K. Gandhi.

63-065.r: Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India → Champaran 1917; among given options, earliest is Ahmedabad (February-March 1918) over low wages/plague bonus, where he first used hunger strike.

63-067.r: Gandhi's first major public speech in India → opening of Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi, February 1916.

63-068.r: Gandhi launched his mission of freeing bonded labour from Patna, on his way to Champaran with Rajkumar Shukla (against forced indigo farming).
63-068.c: Answer not printed (*); explanation points to Patna.

63-069.r: Ahmedabad Satyagraha (1918) → industrial (cotton mill) workers vs mill owners over plague bonus; Gandhi advised strike.

63-072.r: Trusteeship principle → propounded in South Africa, 1903 (Gandhi's law firm in Johannesburg, lived there till 1910).

63-073.r: Gandhian economy: non-violent; centralisation breeds exploitation; against mechanisation in India; but never opposed mechanisation in USA (economy should suit each country).

63-074.r: Gandhi: socio-economic uplift of untouchables → cottage/rural industries (khadi, handlooms, sericulture, handicrafts).

63-075.r: 'Gandhian Innovation' (coined by Prof. Prahlad and R.A. Mashelkar) → produce more from less input for more people.

63-076.r: First event → Champaran Satyagraha (1917); then Kheda (1918), Non-Cooperation (1920), Civil Disobedience (1930).
